import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_0.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_1.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_2.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_3.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_4.csv"
    ]

    # Read all source CSV files into a list of DataFrames
    # Use index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column as per Hint 24
    dfs = [pd.read_csv(f, index_col=0) for f in source_files]

    # All source tables have the exact same schema as the target:
    # ['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']
    # So we can simply concatenate (union) all source tables vertically.

    # Concatenate all source DataFrames
    combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # Ensure columns are in the exact order and type as target schema
    target_columns = ['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']
    combined_df = combined_df[target_columns]

    # According to the target examples:
    # - Year is string (e.g. "1978 (51st)")
    # - Category is string
    # - Nominee is string
    # - Movie is string, but note it contains movie title plus a string like {'Name'} in braces
    # - Winner is string, values like "NO" or presumably "YES"

    # We will ensure all columns are string type to match target schema
    for col in target_columns:
        combined_df[col] = combined_df[col].astype(str)

    # Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
    output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
